Eval 0 (wall) both configs scored 5/5 this iteration because audit output was pre-embedded — the primary blocker from iter 1 (Bash permissions) was removed. With-skill still used 20% fewer tokens (38k vs 48k) and took 23% less time (127s vs 165s).
Eval 1 (pipe) remains non-discriminating — both configs pass 4/4 identically. Replace with a cartridge seeded with a CRITICAL flag so the PASS eval actually tests triage skill.

Eval 2 (mezzanine) shows the persistent advantage: without-skill repeated its iter-1 failure of skipping phys validation, even with stale jCodemunch data showing obviously wrong values. Skill explicitly lists valid MASTER_MAT_DB keys in Section C1.

Key change vs iter 1: FUZZ_CRASH gap is now addressed — the skill's Family B classification table and AUDIT-first mandate meant the with-skill agent correctly ordered B→A. Without-skill agent found the crash too (because audit was pre-loaded), but took 2x the tool calls (23 vs 11).
Next improvement opportunity: Eval 1 needs a better test case. Consider a cartridge with a single seeded CRITICAL_LOOSE_VERTS or FUZZ_CRASH so the pipe eval actually discriminates.
